pull.title: test: handle mainnet logs in `combine_logs.py`
pull.body:
**Problem:** Running `combine_logs.py` on the logs from a mainnet functional test such as `rpc_validateaddress.py` raises `AttributeError`. The helper expects a path like `node0/regtest/debug.log`, but mainnet writes `node0/debug.log`.

Before #16973, the helper silently skipped the mainnet log. That PR made the search recursive, so it finds the log and then fails when the regex tries to extract a subdirectory.

**Fix:** Get the log directory relative to `node0/` from the path the script already found.

<details>
<summary>Manual reproducer</summary>

From the repository root with a functional-test build:

```bash
dir=$(mktemp -d)
build/test/functional/rpc_validateaddress.py --tmpdir="$dir/run" --nocleanup
test/functional/combine_logs.py "$dir/run"
```

The address-validation test passes. Before the fix, the last command fails in `read_logs()`:

```text
  File "test/functional/combine_logs.py", line 88, in read_logs
    chain = re.search(r'node0/(.+?)/debug\.log$', debug_logs[0].as_posix()).group(1)
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'group'
```

With the fix, the same command prints both the `test` and `node0` log entries in timestamp order.
</details>

test: handle mainnet logs in combine_logs.py

Mainnet functional tests write debug.log directly under node0/.
The helper used to skip that log, but since #16973, the recursive glob finds it, but the regex still expects a chain subdirectory and raises AttributeError.

Derive the relative directory from the discovered path so the helper can include the mainnet node log in its output.

events.body: If this is broken, that seems like more reason to remove entirely, rather than fix: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36958#issuecomment-7138986376.

> If this is broken, that seems like more reason to remove entirely, rather than fix: [#36958 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36958#issuecomment-7138986376).

Was wondering about the same, closing and +1 for removal

This is used by the test runner, it can't be removed:

```
test/functional/test_runner.py:                    combined_logs_args = [sys.executable, os.path.join(tests_dir, 'combine_logs.py'), testdir]
Yea, sorry. This can be fixed (and backported).

Code Review ACK 4e1dc2e01511ef9328a54fbbf756cb8c159898a7

I use `combine_logs.py` often, but apparently never with a mainnet test.

Special constellations such as `feature_config_args.py` (multiple chains for one node) and `wallet_crosschain.py` (mixed chains) will still not behave ideally, but I don't think this is worth fixing - it seems good enough for me.
